attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No available lower-bound method rules out arbitrary selected-image separators B_t. These labelers need not be SAT algorithms, so the target SAT hardness hypothesis does not exclude them.
steps: Fix an ensemble of R selectors A_t, each producing s indices into the N^q generated SAT queries.
For each pair (t,u), build a circuit that computes j=A_t(x,u), then y=G_N(x,j), then the selected-image label B_t(y).
OR all R*s outputs. By the separation promise, this computes H_N on all x outside E_N.
Hardwire the exceptional inputs by equality gates and override the answer on E_N, with cost N|E_N| up to subpolynomial factors.
The resulting circuit has size at most R*s*(N^a+N^rho+N^b) plus exception cost, giving N^{r+ell+max{a,rho,b}+o(1)}+N^{1+delta+o(1)}.
Therefore any claimed N^{1+epsilon} lower bound for H_N is valid only if every such separating ensemble exceeds the same exponent threshold.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a route-level upper-bound audit and falsifier criterion. It does not prove C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon}, and therefore does not prove SAT notin P/poly or P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: one-sided separating-ensemble leakage gate

assumptions: Constants q,rho,r,ell,a,b,delta,epsilon are fixed independently of N, and d>1 is fixed.
The generator family G_N has nonuniform circuit size at most N^rho and outputs well-formed SAT instances of length L=(log N)^d.
There are R<=N^r selectors, each with list length s<=N^ell and circuit size at most N^a.
The label circuits B_t have size at most N^b and are charged as arbitrary nonuniform leakage, not as valid SAT solvers.
The exception set E_N is hardwired by equality tests, costing N^{1+delta+o(1)} gates.
definitions: source object: generated-OR carrier H_N on N input bits, H_N(x)=OR_{j<N^q} SAT(G_N(x,j)) with output length L=(log N)^d.
target object: SAT on L-bit formulas and the target consequence SAT notin P/poly, with NP not subset P/poly only after the length-cover transfer is certified.
controlled interface: replace each generated SAT query by a hypothetical SAT circuit of size L^c, while charging generator size N^rho and fanout M=N^q.
target-preserving condition: d>1, q<1+epsilon, rho<1+epsilon, no nonuniform advice enters G_N beyond its charged circuit, and N ranges cover all SAT input lengths.
A_t is a selector circuit of size at most N^a; on input x and list position u<s it outputs an index j<N^q.
B_t is a selected-image label circuit on L-bit formulas; it need not decide SAT outside formulas actually selected by A_t and G_N.
Separation means that for every x outside E_N, H_N(x)=1 iff some pair (t,u) has B_t(G_N(x,A_t(x,u)))=1.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Refines the source-side audit: the lower-bound obligation is not merely against exact list selectors or promise SAT solvers, but against arbitrary selected-image separators.
candidate_lemmas.statement: One-sided separating-ensemble falsifier for generated-OR magnification. Let H_N(x)=OR_{j<N^q} SAT(G_N(x,j)) with |x|=N, |G_N(x,j)|=L=(log N)^d, and C(G_N)<=N^rho. If positives and negatives of H_N, outside |E_N|<=N^delta exceptions, are separated by R=N^r selector circuits each outputting s=N^ell indices and by selected-image label circuits of size N^b, then C(H_N)<=N^{r+ell+max{a,rho,b}+o(1)}+N^{1+delta+o(1)}. Hence a valid N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound must rule out every such separator with r+ell+max{a,rho,b}<1+epsilon and delta<epsilon.

d>1, so L^c=(log N)^{dc}=N^{o(1)}.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No gap for total explicit separators; the blocking gap is applying the lemma to partial, advised, oracle, or algebraic-extension carriers that never produce such an F_N.
steps: Fix m, N=2^m, y_N=tt(SAT_m), and a total explicit separator F_N for SIZE(m^k).
Assume \widetilde{deg}_{1/3}(F_N)<=t. For any input with b disjoint sensitive blocks, restrict F_N to those blocks; the induced total b-bit function has approximate degree Omega(sqrt(b)).
Therefore bs(F_N)<=O(t^2) by the Nisan-Szegedy approximate-degree lower bound for total Boolean functions.
Use C(F_N)<=bs(F_N)^2, so the SAT input y_N has a one-certificate of size O(t^4).
The subcube fixed by that certificate lies inside F_N^{-1}(1), giving density at least 2^{-O(t^4)}.
If t^4=O(log N), F_N^{-1}(1) is poly(N)-constructive, polynomially large, and useful against the same SIZE(m^k) target.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation classifies a proof object as natural and hence barrier-exposed; it does not prove SAT lower bounds and does not settle P != NP.

assumptions: F_N is total on all N-bit strings, not merely defined on SAT and small-circuit truth tables.
The approximating polynomial has worst-case error at most 1/3 on all of {0,1}^N.
Constructivity means a uniform algorithm decides F_N(x) in N^{O(1)} time from x alone.
Usefulness is against the named nonuniform target SIZE(m^k), not an average or heuristic target.
Known total-function inequalities \widetilde{deg}(F)=Omega(sqrt(bs(F))) and C(F)<=bs(F)^2 are allowed.
definitions: source object: a total Boolean separator family F_N on truth tables of length N=2^m, decidable in poly(N) time and approximable pointwise within error 1/3 by degree t real polynomials.
target object: a Razborov-Rudich natural property R_N subset {0,1}^N that contains tt(SAT_m), excludes tt(C) for every m-input circuit C of size m^k, and has density N^{-O(1)}.
controlled interface: approximate-degree lower-bound method -> total natural property via Nisan-Szegedy approximate-degree/block-sensitivity lower bound and certificate-complexity upper bound.
target-preserving condition: totality, no advice leakage, poly(N) constructivity, universal rejection of SIZE(m^k) truth tables, and t^4=O(log N) are all preserved in truth-table coordinates.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A claimed counterexample must be a total explicit useful separator with t=O((log N)^{1/4}) but density below every N^{-A}; otherwise the falsifier is really failure of totality, usefulness, constructivity, or the threshold.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Bridge lemma converting low approximate degree of a total explicit separator into natural-proof largeness; it is route-level barrier control, not evidence for P != NP.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Approximate-degree naturalization gate. Let N=2^m and y_N=tt(SAT_m). If a total poly(N)-constructive Boolean property F_N:{0,1}^N->{0,1} satisfies F_N(y_N)=1, rejects every truth table of every m-input circuit of size at most m^k, and has \widetilde{deg}_{1/3}(F_N)<=t, then R_N=F_N^{-1}(1) is a constructive property useful against SIZE(m^k) with density at least 2^{-O(t^4)}. Thus t=O((log N)^{1/4}) makes the route a valid natural-proof object, subject to the PRF falsifier.

assumptions: Circuit truth tables are counted by circuit descriptions of length O(s log s) with s=m^k.
The promise approximant is not assumed bounded or accurate outside D_N.
Natural-proof largeness is measured in the full cube {0,1}^N.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the proof uses only D_N-correctness and then infers polynomial density, the sparse promise domain is the falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quarantine lemma preventing a promise low-degree argument from being mistaken for a natural property or a P vs NP route.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Promise approximate degree is an escape only after quarantine. A low-degree approximant on D_N={y_N} union TT(SIZE(m^k)) alone does not imply largeness, because D_N is exponentially sparse in the truth-table cube. To invoke ADG-29.1 the route must give a total poly(N)-constructive extension G_N agreeing on D_N with \widetilde{deg}(G_N)^4=O(log N), or else a direct polynomial-density accepting set disjoint from the target.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The bridge is valid, but the route still lacks a constructed low-D, cap-compatible, non-natural MCSP source with sound existential hard images.
steps: Enumerate all O(m)-bit accepted certificates, emit their tables, and merge duplicates by exhaustive equality; this stays within 2^{O(m)} time for constant D and linear certificates.
Define M_m(z,x) as the value of the z-th distinct emitted table on x, using zero for out-of-range z; then M_m has input length at most (1+D)m+o(m).
If M_m had circuits below 2^{epsilon m-o(m)}, hardwiring the index of a hard emitted image would give a small circuit for that MCSP no-side table, contradiction.
Use the uniform kappa-dense source schedule and padding by ignored bits to define one E language on all large lengths, losing only the factor kappa in the exponent.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a conditional route-level transfer theorem. It does not prove P != NP because the source object may be as hard to construct as the desired lower bound.

assumptions: For each source length m in a uniform kappa-dense set S, some accepted emitted table has circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m}.
The number B_m of distinct emitted accepted tables is at most 2^{D m+o(m)} with constant D.
Duplicate emitted tables are quotientable by full truth-table equality in 2^{O(m)} time; no nonuniform representative selector is used.
Circuit lower bounds are against nonuniform fan-in two Boolean circuits; the constructed target language must lie in E.
definitions: source object: uniform MCSP certificate emitter V_m with O(m)-bit certificates, E-time stream emission of m-input truth tables, image entropy D, source threshold 2^{epsilon m}, and verifier cap alpha_V.
target object: an E-uniform multiplexed and padded language L_D with Boolean circuit lower bound 2^{delta n} at all sufficiently large target lengths.
controlled interface: canonical distinct-image enumeration maps an image index z and input x to the z-th emitted truth-table value; kappa-padding transfers source lengths to target lengths.
target-preserving condition: enumeration, length schedule, and padding are uniform; epsilon<=alpha_V; certificate length is O(m); and no advice chooses the hard image.
